entities.summary: Father Francisco Noronha was a Spanish physician and botanist who resided for some time at Manila, Luzon, Philippines, where he took much effort to organize the Royal Botanic Garden and stock it with valuable plants. Three sets of his water-colour drawings of Javan plants and one set of 108 numbered drawings still exist. Williams (2003) describes him as "a Spanish physician and botanist who had visited Madagascar", while Zuidervaart & Van Gent (2004) call him "a capable botanist from Manila" who in 1786 had taken over supervision of the museum of the Batavian Society of Arts and Sciences in Java.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Francisco Noronha's work on organizing the Royal Botanic Garden in Manila and his contributions to the field of botany had a significant regional impact, particularly in Southeast Asia. His legacy can be seen in the continued study and conservation of plant species in the region.
